summary: Herkimer County, NY fire tower: 1919 Aermotor LS40 on Moose River Mountain, closed after 1970, removed 1977; site lies in the Ha-de-ron-dah Wilderness Area with a trail to it.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor LS40 steel tower (Forest Lookouts gives 47 ft)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1977; no source describes what, if anything, remains on the summit

visit.trail_note: CNY Hiking lists an old trail to the site of the former fire tower; a 2013 blog describes the approach through hunting-club property before the wilderness gate

events.note: Conservation Commission bought a steel tower and erected it on Moose River Mountain (Wikipedia: 60 ft; Forest Lookouts: 47 ft)
Tower moved from the earlier Lewis County site to Moose River Mountain, Town of Webb, Herkimer County
New cabin built for the observer's living quarters
Closed at the end of the 1970 season, per NYSFFLA and Wikipedia; Forest Lookouts says staffed into the mid-1970s
Removed because it was deemed excess to fire detection needs; classed as a non-conforming structure in the new Ha-de-ron-dah Wilderness Area

corrections.why: Wikipedia, the NYSFFLA entry and Starr's list all give 60 ft (18.3 m); the 47-ft (14.3 m) figure comes only from the Forest Lookouts page

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts says 47 ft; Wikipedia, NYSFFLA and Starr's list say 60 ft. The story gives 60 ft and says the sources disagree.
Forest Lookouts says staffed into the mid-1970s; NYSFFLA and Wikipedia say closed at the end of the 1970 season. The story says the sources differ.
Starr's list gives 1911 / 1918 for the station; NYSFFLA and Wikipedia date the steel tower to 1919. The story uses 1919.

notes_for_editor: The record height (14.3 m, 47 ft) comes only from Forest Lookouts; three sources say 60 ft, so the correction is proposed, not applied. Starr's list gives 1911 / 1918 and seems to place a 1912 wooden station on this mountain, which NYSFFLA and Wikipedia contradict (they put it at a Lewis County site); not used. No source states public access. The 2013 blog describes the approach through hunting-club land, so access was left unset for review. Trail length differs (CNY Hiking lists 0.7 miles to the site; the blog describes a longer hike); only the trail's existence is used. A Herkimer County Historical Society Facebook post and an FFLA-NY Facebook hike post were seen only in search snippets; not used.
